title: Observability standup + sprint synopsis (tracing, dashboards, cost telemetry) - 2026-03-05
content:
Week snapshot (Mar 2 - Mar 6, 2026)

Purpose: capture standup notes, decisions, and action items for tracing, dashboard hygiene, and cost telemetry experiments. This doc is a working sprint synopsis — expect follow-ups and PRs next week.

High-level highlights:
- Small production incident on Tue (partial trace retention gap for low-priority services) — mitigated by temporary retention-extension flag. Root cause: roll-forward of a new retention policy without corresponding index migration (OBS-1724).
- Agreed to pilot dynamic sampling by service to reduce trace ingestion costs; scoped 2-week canary for 4 non-critical services.
- Dashboard refresh pushed: replaced five legacy panels that queried large unpartitioned tables with pre-aggregations; estimated query cost reduction ~42% for those panels.

Standup logs (daily, key points only):
Mon 2026-03-02:
- Aisha: finished Tempo ingestion backfill prototype; needs review. Blocker: missing migration script for span_metadata index.
- Marco: exploring dynamic sampling config format; prototyped service-policy JSON and a dynamic sampler that sets sampling probability by QPS and error-rate.
- Priya: triaging retention incident. Launched retention-extension flag for affected services.
- Liam: dashboard cost audit — identified 12 heavy queries across three dashboards (trace-heatmap, latency-by-route, token-cost-over-time).

Tue 2026-03-03:
- Incident response: partial retention gap on low-priority traces surfaced (OBS-1724). Temporary fix applied; team agreed migration run Thu night.
- Chen: finalized BigQuery cost query (saved as cost-telemetry/cost-by-dashboard.sql) and shared initial numbers: trace ingestion accounts for ~26% of observability spend last month.
- Action: create canary list for dynamic sampling (see action item A1).

Wed 2026-03-04:
- Design huddle: sampling policy decisions. Key points: sample by service with tiered weights, allow per-endpoint overrides, preserve 100% sampling for spans with error tag (status >= 500). Agreed on metrics to monitor: missed-error-rate, tail-latency-slo-breach, and sampling-coverage.
- Marco to open PR for sampler config and server-side implementation (linked: PR #842).
- Dashboard refactor merged to staging; performance improvement observed in staging queries.

Thu 2026-03-05:
- Migration window scheduled 03/05 23:00 UTC for span_metadata index. Migration checklist prepared and dry-run done in dev.
- Canary services selected: session-service, uploads-service, notifications-service, search-lite. Canary owners assigned.
- Action: create rollback playbook and SLI alarms for sampling changes (A3).

Fri 2026-03-06:
- Post-migration verification: span_metadata index migrated successfully in production for the affected partitions. Follow-up: spot-check scripts to validate retention across 30-day windows (A5).
- Cost telemetry: first snapshot after dashboard changes shows 38% drop in query billing for the replaced panels; still pending full-month projection.
- Quick retro: team happy with faster iteration but we need clearer pre-merge cost estimates for dashboard changes.

Decisions made this week:
1) Dynamic sampling pilot approved. Scope: 4 canary services, 2-week run, automatic rollback if missed-error-rate increases by >1% absolute or tail-latency-SLO breaches by >0.5%. (JIRA-OBS-1729)
2) Dashboard pre-aggregation pattern standard adopted for high-cardinality trace panels. New dashboard guideline doc to be added to confluence.
3) Retention policy change workflow updated: migrations must include a preflight check and a 24-hour hold window before cutover.

Action items (owner, due):
- A1: Marco — create canary sampling config and PR (due 2026-03-08). Linked PR #842.
- A2: Aisha — finish tempo ingestion backfill and migration script for span_metadata index (due 2026-03-07).
- A3: Priya + SRE oncall — produce rollback playbook and SLO-based alarms for sampling pilot (due 2026-03-09).
- A4: Liam — complete dashboard cost audit spreadsheet and tag heavy panels for refactor (due 2026-03-10).
- A5: Chen — write spot-check verification scripts for retention migration and schedule an automated run (due 2026-03-12).

Runbook / ops notes:
- If sampling pilot triggers rollback conditions, runbook step: set global sampler to service-default-100% and notify oncall -> create rollback PR to remove sampler rule from config -> redeploy config -> run verification job. Estimated full rollback time: 12-18 min.
- Post-migration verification command (ad-hoc):
  bq query --use_legacy_sql=false "SELECT service, COUNT(1) as spans, MAX(timestamp) as last_ts FROM observability.traces_partitioned WHERE partition_date >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 30 DAY) GROUP BY service ORDER BY spans DESC LIMIT 20"
- Grafana debug tips: use 'explain query' on panels to check if pre-aggregations are used; toggle time range to isolate heavy queries.

Metrics / quick numbers (snapshots) — Mar 5 production pre/post changes:
- Trace ingestion cost (30d rolling) pre-change: $14,800/mo estimated. Post panel refactor: estimated $9,200/mo (partial; need full-month projection).
- Sampled traces ingest rate (current): ~420k spans/day. Expected after 2-week canary (estimated): 260k-310k spans/day depending on service weights.
- Dashboard heavy panel reductions: 5 panels replaced with pre-aggregations; avg query latency down 48% in staging.

Open questions / TODOs:
- What should be the default sampling floor for low-traffic services? (proposal: min 0.1%)
- How to expose sampled vs unsampled traffic to downstream metrics pipelines to keep cardinality stable?
- Need cost estimator for proposed sampling rules (quick spreadsheet exists but needs validation).

Notes for next week:
- Start canary rollout for dynamic sampling (monitoring and alarms first).
- Complete PR reviews for sampler and tempo backfill.
- Finish dashboard audit and present cost-savings plan to engineering leadership.

Meeting attachments / references:
- cost-telemetry/cost-by-dashboard.sql (BigQuery draft)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/842
- JIRA: JIRA-OBS-1724 (retention migration), JIRA-OBS-1729 (sampling pilot)

Quick logbook (short-hand):
- 03/02: tempo backfill prototyped; retention gap found.
- 03/03: migration scheduling + cost query landed.
- 03/04: sampling config design; PR opened.
- 03/05: migration ran successfully.
- 03/06: dashboard cost snapshot validated; canary list finalized.

If you want a short distilled deck for leadership: I can prepare a 2-slide summary (cost impact + risk/mitigation) by Tue 2026-03-09.

-- Priya Kapoor (owner)
